title: PMBJP drug-code identity is unverifiable for committed product-presentation mappings
runtime_risk_rationale: Mapping resolution keys on product_id (a content hash of the catalogue product row) and revalidates product_assertion_sha256, returning status "stale" on drift. The PMBJP code is descriptive metadata in mapping_id and in the pmbjp-tender evidence identifier, not the resolution key, so a wrong code cannot mis-resolve onto a different drug at runtime.
evidence_chain_risk_rationale: Each mapping's review evidence cites pmbjp-tender:RC-<n>/<year>:<code>:page-<n>. If the code denotes a different product in the source document, the clinician approved against a citation pointing at the wrong tender row.

root_cause.summary: Our own 2026-07-07 text extraction paired the drug-code column to the product-name column positionally. The PMBJP list is a Word table in which many name cells render on a separate line from their serial/code cell, so a positional zip drifts wherever that happens - assigning names to the wrong codes. Same document, wrong codes.

source_document.note: Unchanged since the adapter was written (git history shows the URL was never edited, only made env-overridable). PDF CreationDate 2026-02-06, produced by Microsoft Word 2021.

proof.method: Read PDF page 62 directly and compared it to the catalogue.
proof.conclusion: The real table uses every other code in this region (2138, 2140, 2142, 2144, 2146), with 2139/2141/2143/2145 carrying names that render lower (Zinc Sulphate, Pyridostigmine, Budesonide, Combikit). Zipping the name stream onto the code stream in order reproduces the catalogue exactly, including Pyridostigmine landing on 2144. That is a positional-pairing artifact, not an edition difference.

root_cause.what_is_actually_wrong: Only the drug-code LABEL. Product identity is sound: product_id hashes brand name, manufacturer, pack, form and ingredients, none of which came from the code column. All 17 committed mappings therefore bind the correct products; what is mislabelled is the code in mapping_id and in the pmbjp-tender evidence citation.

verification_run.checked_against: official PMBJP product list (PIB attachment, adapter default URL), retrieved 2026-07-27

remediation_completed: The janaushadhi adapter now writes pmbjp.provenance.json recording origin, source_url, pdf_sha256, pdf_byte_count and an explicit code_space_verifiable flag, so a future catalogue snapshot is attributable to an exact source document.
A text-only cache with no recoverable PDF is recorded as code_space_verifiable:false rather than silently assumed correct - precisely the state the current snapshot is in.

Added src/cli/verify-pmbjp-mapping-codes.mjs (npm run verify:pmbjp-mapping-codes), which checks every committed mapping code against a named, hashed source list and exits non-zero when any code cannot be confirmed.
remediation_outstanding: Make the janaushadhi extraction geometry-aware (e.g. pdftotext -bbox or table-cell extraction) so each product name is paired to its own drug code rather than zipped positionally. 632 of 2111 rows are affected in the current document.
Add a parser self-check that fails closed when the number of parsed rows does not equal the number of serial numbers present in the document (1466 parsed vs 2111 serials today).
Rebuild the catalogue with the corrected extractor and the new provenance capture, then re-run npm run verify:pmbjp-mapping-codes to confirm all 17 mapping codes.
Correct the code labels in the affected mapping_ids and their pmbjp-tender citations, which is a clinician-review action because the citations are part of the approved evidence.

rebuild_assessment.question: Should the PMBJP catalogue be rebuilt now, so drug codes become verifiable against a recorded source?
rebuild_assessment.verdict_reason: Rebuilding from the adapter default source today would destroy more than it repairs.
rebuild_assessment.preflight_method: product_id is a content hash of (brand_name, manufacturer, pack_label, form_raw, ingredient signature) and is independent of the drug code. Parsing the current official list, deriving product_id for every row, and intersecting with the 17 committed mapping product_ids shows exactly which mappings a rebuild would preserve.
proof_that_codes_are_edition_scoped: Warfarin Tablets IP 1mg: code 2141 in the catalogue edition, code 2144 in the current official list.
Fluconazole Tablets IP 150 mg: code 1246 in the catalogue edition, code 1252 in the current list.
Voriconazole Tablets IP 200mg: code 2034 in the catalogue edition, code 2033 in the current list.
Tramadol Prolonged Release Tablets IP 100 mg: code 521 in the catalogue edition, code 519 in the current list.
The same product, identical content hash, different drug code. This is direct proof that a PMBJP code is only meaningful against a named source document.
why_the_right_source_is_not_available: The adapter default (PIB attachment) currently serves 1466 rows; the 2026-07-07 catalogue holds 2111 janaushadhi rows, so the catalogue was built from a larger, different document.

The source the mapping evidence actually cites (janaushadhi.gov.in product MRP list) is a React single-page app. Its public product endpoint, janaushadhi.gov.in:8443/api/v1/website/getAllProductForWeb, returned HTTP 500 for GET and for POST with the usual pagination shapes. No list could be retrieved. Probing was stopped after five requests rather than continuing to hammer a government endpoint.
data/raw/janaushadhi is empty and dist/latest records no PMBJP source URL or hash, so the original edition cannot be reconstructed locally.
what_would_make_a_rebuild_safe: Obtain a PMBJP product list that is at least as complete as the catalogue snapshot (>= 2111 rows) from a citable official source, and record its URL and sha256 via the new provenance capture.
Re-run the rebuild-impact preflight against that document and confirm all 17 committed mapping product_ids are preserved before rebuilding.
Then run npm run verify:pmbjp-mapping-codes against that same pinned document and re-verify the tender page citations for any mapping whose code moved.
rebuild_assessment.interim_position: No rebuild. The catalogue, the 17 mappings and the 7 promoted rules are left exactly as they are: internal-evaluation only, content-hash bound, fail-closed on drift, with production-open empty. New PMBJP product mappings remain blocked. This is a stable and safe resting state; the unverifiable code citations are recorded here rather than silently accepted.
rebuild_assessment.superseded_note: The earlier verdict assumed a better source document was needed and unobtainable. That was wrong: the correct document is in hand and unchanged. What is needed is a geometry-aware extraction that pairs each name cell to its own code cell, after which the catalogue can be rebuilt with correct codes and provenance recorded.

root_cause_superseded.original_claim: PMBJP drug codes are not stable across product-list editions, and the catalogue was built from a different, larger edition that is now unrecoverable.
root_cause_superseded.why_retracted: Traced to the source. The catalogue was built from the SAME document the adapter still points at. That document contains exactly 2111 serial-numbered products, matching the catalogue's 2111 janaushadhi rows exactly. There is no missing edition.

corrected_codes.method: Looked each mapped product name up among the 1479 correctly-paired rows of the current extraction, where a name sits on the same line as its own drug code.

directly_correctable.product: Tramadol Prolonged Release Tablets IP 100 mg

corrected_codes.note: These 10 products sit on rows whose name is orphaned from its code in the current extraction, so their true code cannot be read positionally either. They require a geometry-aware extraction (pdftotext -bbox, or reading the table cells) to pair name cells to code cells reliably.
